title: DICOM 2026c selected VL WSI rule-family, IOD and requirement-statement challenge profile
excluded_capabilities: LABEL, OVERVIEW, and THUMBNAIL image flavors
multiple optical paths or focal planes
calibrated color transformation and scanner-profile accuracy
Context Group (CID) and Defined Term constraints

value constraints stated only in prose, such as Bits Stored equal to Bits Allocated, Specimen Label in Image fixed by Image Type, or Number of Optical Paths equal to the Optical Path Sequence Item count
conditions that cannot be determined from the object, which are counted and never failed
files with an absent or unrecognized Transfer Syntax UID, which the evaluated engine cannot open
exhaustive normative completeness beyond the generated VL WSI IOD requirement tables

requirements.statement: The Patient Module is present; Patient Name, Patient ID, Patient Birth Date, and Patient Sex are present even when empty.
The General Study Module is present with a valid Study Instance UID and its Type 2 Study Date, Study Time, Referring Physician Name, Study ID, and Accession Number attributes.
The General Series and Whole Slide Microscopy Series Modules are present with a valid Series Instance UID, Modality SM, and Series Number present.
The Frame of Reference Module is present for VOLUME images, with a valid Frame of Reference UID and Position Reference Indicator present.
The General and Enhanced General Equipment Modules identify the manufacturer, model, device serial number, and software version with non-empty values.
The General Acquisition Module is present and the acquisition timing required by the WSI specialization is coherent.
The General Image Module is present and its image identification, instance number, burned-in annotation, and lossy-history semantics are valid.
The Microscope Slide Layer Tile Organization Module completely describes a TILED_FULL total pixel matrix, its origin, orientation, and one focal plane.
The Image Pixel Module contains valid rows, columns, sample count, photometric interpretation, bit depth, pixel representation, and pixel data.
Acquisition Context Sequence is present; it may contain zero items when no acquisition context is asserted.
The Multi-frame Functional Groups Module supplies shared Pixel Measures and per-frame Frame Content, Plane Position (Slide), and Optical Path Identification as required for every frame.
The Multi-frame Dimension Module defines dimension organization and index pointers whose order and per-frame values agree.
The Specimen Module identifies the microscope-slide container and specimen and preserves required issuer and preparation-sequence presence.
The Whole Slide Microscopy Image Module satisfies all core VOLUME conditions for dimensions, pixels, acquisition, presentation, focusing, and compression history.
The Optical Path Module declares exactly one identifiable path, its illumination semantics, frame reference, and required ICC profile for color.
The SOP Common Module identifies the VL WSI SOP Class and a valid SOP Instance consistently with File Meta Information.
Common-instance and source references, when present, resolve to the correct SOP Class and Instance without self-reference or contradictions.
When a multi-resolution pyramid is supplied, its Pyramid UID, layer geometry, physical extent, origin, orientation, specimen, and container identity agree across instances.
Image Type contains exactly ORIGINAL or DERIVED, PRIMARY, VOLUME, and NONE or RESAMPLED.
VOLUME images contain positive Imaged Volume Width, Height, and Depth, and width and height agree with pixel spacing and total-matrix dimensions.
Samples per Pixel and Photometric Interpretation agree with each other and with the transfer syntax; Planar Configuration is present and zero for color.
Number of Frames, Bits Allocated, Bits Stored, High Bit, and unsigned Pixel Representation are valid for the core images.
Acquisition DateTime is present and non-empty.
Lossy Image Compression is present and truthful, with required method and ratio values paired when lossy history is declared.
MONOCHROME2 images contain IDENTITY Presentation LUT Shape, Rescale Intercept 0, and Rescale Slope 1.
Volumetric Properties is VOLUME, Specimen Label in Image is NO, and Burned In Annotation is NO.
Focus Method is AUTO or MANUAL, Extended Depth of Field is NO, and extended-depth focal-plane count and spacing attributes are not required by the declared profile.
Dimension Organization Type is TILED_FULL; Total Pixel Matrix Rows and Columns are positive; Total Pixel Matrix Focal Planes is one; and all expected tile positions are encoded exactly once.
Total Pixel Matrix Origin Sequence has one item with finite X and Y offsets and, when present, a finite Z offset.
Image Orientation (Slide) contains six finite direction cosines whose row and column vectors are unit length and orthogonal.
Dimension index pointers and values correspond in order to each frame's row and column positions in the total pixel matrix.
Number of Optical Paths is one and matches the single Optical Path Sequence item, whose identifier is non-empty and unique.
Illumination Type Code Sequence is present and contains at least one coded illumination method.
Each optical path has either a positive Illumination Wave Length or one-item Illumination Color Code Sequence.
The Optical Path Identification functional group references the declared Optical Path Identifier.
Every non-MONOCHROME2 optical path contains a structurally valid input-device ICC profile with a color space compatible with stored samples.
Container Identifier is present and non-empty.
Issuer of the Container Identifier Sequence is present with zero or one structurally valid issuer item.
Container Type Code Sequence identifies a microscope slide and Specimen Description Sequence contains at least one specimen item.
Each specimen item has a non-empty Specimen Identifier and globally valid Specimen UID whose scope remains consistent across the set.
Specimen Preparation Sequence is present even when empty; every present preparation item contains a non-empty Preparation Step Content Item Sequence.
Patient identity is consistent within a Study; Series maps to one Study and Frame of Reference; and a Frame of Reference maps to one patient, Study, container, and issuer.
A Specimen UID resolves consistently to one Specimen Identifier and issuer scope across all instances.
File Meta and data-set SOP identities agree, and a SOP Instance UID is not reused for divergent instance identity.
All layers sharing a Pyramid UID have the same physical extent, total-matrix origin, and slide orientation.
Native and encapsulated Pixel Data structure, frame count, fragments, basic offsets, extended offsets, and extended lengths are coherent with the selected transfer syntax.
Every selected frame decodes to the declared rows, columns, sample count, and bit depth.
When derivation or source references are present, referenced SOP Class and Instance identities are correct and do not create self-reference.
The shared WSI Image Frame Type functional group is present and agrees with Image Type.
An image derived from another SOP Instance includes the Derivation Image functional group with coded derivation and source references.
The Type 1 Content Date is present.
Each Module of Table A.32.8-1 is present when its Usage is M or its usage condition requires it, and absent when its usage condition forbids it.

Only Functional Group Macros of Table A.32.8-2 are used; the mandatory Pixel Measures and Whole Slide Microscopy Image Frame Type Macros apply to every Frame and are Shared; Frame Content is not Shared; and no Macro is in both the Shared and Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequences.
A present Per-Frame Functional Groups Sequence has exactly one Item per Frame.
Top-level Type 1 Attributes of the applicable Modules are present with a Value, and Type 2 Attributes are present.

Type 1C and 2C Attributes are present, and Type 1C with a Value, when their condition is met, and absent when it is not unless the condition permits presence; conditions the object cannot determine are not failed.
Attribute Types and conditions are evaluated within every Sequence Item, including nested Code Sequence Items and Shared and Per-Frame Functional Group Items.
Attributes with Enumerated Values, including per-Value and conditional Enumerated Values and Attributes in Sequence and Functional Group Items, carry only the listed Values.
In explicit VR Transfer Syntaxes every public Data Element, at any nesting level, is encoded with a VR that PS3.6 specifies for it.
Every Data Element, at any nesting level, has a number of Values admitted by its PS3.6 Value Multiplicity.

String Values follow the format, repertoire, and length of their VR: UID components without leading zeros, Gregorian DA, valid TM and DT, uppercase CS, LO without control characters, DS at most 16 bytes, IS at most 12 bytes, and PN component limits.
Sequences whose definition constrains their number of Items contain that number of Items at the top level, in nested Items, and in Functional Group Items.
The File Meta Information contains its Type 1 elements with valid Values, File Meta Information Version 00H 01H, and a Group Length covering the group.
Media Storage SOP Class UID and Media Storage SOP Instance UID equal the SOP Class UID and SOP Instance UID of the Data Set.
Coded entries use the Defined, non-extensible Context Groups, and Content Item trees follow the Defined Templates, that the IOD tables bind.

VL WSI Image and Frame Type have four Values, Specimen Label in Image follows the flavor, Tiles Overlap, Imaged Volume Depth, Position Reference Indicator, optical paths, derivation, pixel spacing and the regular tiling hold.
Constraints between Attributes hold in the Data Set and every Item.
Instances of the evaluated set agree on Frames of Reference, UID roles, Instance Numbers, Specimen Identifiers, Frame Extraction history and patient group arrangements.
Pixel Padding, Pixel Aspect Ratio, Icon Images and palette tables follow their constraints.
Each encapsulated Frame holds one complete codestream of the coding process its Transfer Syntax identifies, agreeing with the Image Pixel Attributes.
The Data Set as encoded in the file's bytes follows PS3.5 element order, VR, length, private block and character set encoding.
